messages:
sophia: FYI I rolled qatr-rerank-3b (QAT-trained then PTQ'd) into the dev eval cluster. Overall NDCG looks fine, but MRR on JA passage tasks dropped ~5%. Anyone familiar with quantization introducing locale-specific MRR-only shifts?

kevin: hmm. do we have per-slice breakdown? short vs long queries, exact-match vs fuzzy?

lia: quick run details:
```bash
python run_eval.py --model qatr-rerank-3b --tasks jp_passage,jp_longpass,en_passage --metrics mrr,ndcg@10 --quant ptq-int8 --cache prefix,kvcache --tokenizer ja_norm_v3 --preproc strip_code=true
```
results: jp_passage MRR -0.051, ndcg@10 -0.004; jp_longpass MRR -0.012; en_passage MRR +0.008

tom: small ndcg shift but notable mrr drop again. suggests top1 swap concentration. Are swaps concentrated in cached responses (kvcache) vs cold runs?

lia: good call. split by cache_state: cold (no prefix) vs warm (prefix cached). cold MRR delta -0.02, warm MRR delta -0.09. So warm runs amplify the drop.

kevin: that points to KV cache/prefix tokenization boundaries interacting badly with quant noise. Maybe cached key/value projections quantized more aggressively in PTQ path. Did QAT replicate the exact inference runtime?

sophia: QAT training used fp32 runtime sim; PTQ step differs on kernel selection. We also flipped fast-cudnn matmul for cache path in runtime config to save latency. Could be kernel differences.

lia: I dug into a sample: query "" (redacted chat tokens) — fp32 picks an exact doc with phrase, quant picks a higher-embedding doc. Raw scores: fp32 top1=4.05, top2=3.92; int8 top1=3.89, top2=3.96.

kevin: can we dump kv-keys for that query and compare quant/fp32? also check fp16 baseline with same kernels.

lia: yes, I exported kv-key hex dumps and cosine similarity of embeddings. fp32/ptq kv-key sim drops to 0.997 for some tokens in the phrase vs 0.999 normal. tiny, but cascades with cached prefix since following tokens rely on previous kv.

ops-bot: perf-alert: runtime kernel fast-cudnn matmul swapped in for model qatr-rerank-3b on 2024-06-01T09:12Z.

lia: flipping kernel to deterministic matmul (slower) on a small shuffle restored MRR to -0.01. So kernel choice + PTQ quant noise seems multiplicative.

kevin: interesting. action items: 1) run PTQ with per-channel vs per-tensor quant to see sensitivity, 2) run FP16 and QAT-deploy with same runtime kernels to isolate training vs runtime kernel effects, 3) add cache-state slice to eval harness and include top1 swap list (limit 100) for localization tasks.

lia: I'll add cache-state slice and generate top1 swap diffs. Also re-run with per-channel PTQ and deterministic matmul.

sophia: if deterministic kernel fixes it we should gate kernel switch behind a canary and not flip globally. We can also backport a micro-A/B that routes 5% of jp traffic to fp16 until we confirm.

kevin: add a small unit test: token-level kv reproducibility for common JP token sequences (dates, place names, kana+kanji combos). Lia please add examples.

lia: adding tests + will open PR for harness slices. Expect initial re-run and swap list by EOD.

eval-bot: Eval finished: qatr-rerank-3b PTQ-int8 (2024-06-01T12:10Z): aggregate NDCG@10 delta -0.004, MRR delta -0.049 on jp_passage. Warm-cache swap rate: 7.2% (72/1000). Deterministic-matmul run: MRR delta -0.009.

sophia: great debugging. Plan: 1) hold rollout, 2) add deterministic matmul as safe fallback for JP canary, 3) continue per-channel PTQ experiments. Will sync in standup. :white_check_mark:
